$comment: ATA chain CUSTODY at verification time — authority.walkChainStructure. A flattened AuthorityLink readout cannot express what the walk checks, so a consumer of one is trusting whoever produced it. The walk consumes presented AtaGrant VCs and refuses what no per-link readout can express: a spliced link (signed by a key that is not the parent's subject), a root issued by someone other than the declared principal, a leaf granted to anyone but the acceptance signer. It then applies the SAME delegation gates linkAttenuates enforces at issuance, plus lifecycle as-of the settlement instant (expiry windows; revocation from the hash-pinned status-list snapshot, never a live dereference). This corpus certifies the STRUCTURAL half — deterministic over presented documents; the cryptographic proof gate (does the proof verify over the grant AS PRESENTED?) is port-injected and proven in the authority package tests, exactly the acceptance split. Outcome discipline is verify's three-way rule: a chain that CONTRADICTS itself is refused (verification-failure); a missing or unwalkable input is not-attempted, never failed, never passed. Key order in `expected` mirrors the outcome objects as constructed; refusal `detail` prose is deliberately not pinned.

cases.name: no chain supplied — a gap, never a proof
an EMPTY chain walks nothing — a placeholder proves no custody
no declared principal — custody has no root to bind to
no acceptance signer — the leaf has nothing to bind to
no settlement instant — lifecycle has no as-of to be evaluated at
an unreadable settlement instant is a gap, not a verdict
a chain element that is not a grant makes the chain unwalkable — a gap, never a failure
a link with no proof cannot establish custody — missing evidence is a gap, not a contradiction
a malformed credentialStatus is a gap — the walk cannot read what revocation state it claims
a status list with no snapshot supplied cannot be checked as-of settlement — never a pass
an unreadable status snapshot is a gap — fail closed, never a pass
a status index beyond the snapshot is unknowable — a gap, never a pass
a root issued by anyone but the declared principal is refused
a root signed by a key that is not its issuer's is refused
a SPLICED middle link — signed by a key that is not the parent's subject — is refused
a link whose STATED issuer is not the parent's subject is refused, even under the right key
the forged empty link {} under a restricting parent is refused — absent is unbounded, not inherited
a link below a NON-DELEGABLE parent is forged, however well its bounds attenuate
a link that mints itself more onward depth than its parent held is refused
a link claiming EXACTLY its parent's depth is refused — the ceiling is parentMaxDepth - 1
a link that OMITS its depth below a depth-bounded parent is refused — omission is the same escalation
a link REVOKED as-of settlement is refused — the bit was set in the pinned snapshot
a link EXPIRED as-of settlement is refused — expiry is lifecycle exactly like revocation
a link not yet valid as-of settlement is refused — validFrom is a gate, not a decoration
a leaf granted to someone other than the acceptance signer is refused — custody ends at the wrong key
a single direct grant to the signer walks — did:pkh binds the scheme-canonical account
a leaf whose subject IS the signer identifier binds exactly — no did:pkh needed, any rail
an unrevoked link with its snapshot walks — the bit was checked and was clear
the two-hop chain — root grant and attenuating delegation — walks to the full readout
the three-hop chain walks when every hop is permitted, continuous, and narrowing
a credentialStatus with no statusPurpose is a gap — the entry names no semantics to apply (Bitstring Status List v1.0 requires it)
a statusPurpose the walk has no semantics for is a gap — never read as revocation, never a pass
an unrevoked link whose entry states statusPurpose revocation walks — the bit was checked and was clear
